project.title: Breast cancer classification
project.alt: Genuine saved-results explorer showing logistic-regression confusion counts, malignant precision and recall, and a training-majority baseline
project.desc: Explore saved classifier errors, compare a training-majority baseline and see why accuracy alone can mislead.
project.built: Turned the reproducible three-model evaluation into an auditable, read-only results lab. Every confusion count and score comes from saved predictions, with a baseline selected only from training labels.
project.why: A high accuracy can hide systematically missed examples when classes are imbalanced. The project makes error types, denominators and evaluation limits visible before interpreting a model comparison.
how: Reproduce the existing fixed three-model evaluation with all 30 features and preprocessing inside training-only cross-validation.
Reconcile saved predictions with source rows, confusion matrices and scores; compute a majority baseline using training labels only.
Choose a saved classifier to explore its errors, malignant precision/recall/F1 and balanced accuracy; controls read results without retraining.
project.demonstrates: Reproducible machine learning, class-imbalance analysis, precise metric interpretation, data-integrity checks and accessible frontend development.
project.caption: Actual browser capture of the saved-results lab after desktop and mobile checks. The controls select previously computed outputs; they do not train a model.
project.result: Measured results are generated from the same source run as the figures.
project.limits: Educational analysis of a public teaching dataset, not a diagnostic system. This browser reads saved results only; it accepts no patient inputs and trains no models. The holdout has been reused across models and portfolio iterations, so it is exploratory rather than an untouched final test or an unbiased selection estimate. The baseline is context, not a new tuned classifier. No independent cohort, clinical validation, calibration study or causal feature interpretation is claimed.
project.technical: A Python export independently reconciles source hashes, fixed partitions, saved prediction labels, confusion counts and metrics before generating the explorer JSON. A training-majority baseline uses 250 benign and 148 malignant training labels. Malignant precision is explicitly undefined when a model predicts no positives; F1 is zero when it misses every positive. The existing evaluation, training-only five-fold CV and figure generation remain unchanged. Browser tests check all four approaches at desktop/mobile widths, keyboard selection, exact rendered values and loading failure.
project.run: Install requirements.txt, run python evaluate.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v, python plot_portfolio.py and python build_explorer.py. Serve docs/ with a local static server. npm ci and npm run test:browser run repeatable desktop/mobile checks. The original notebook remains separate.
gallery: A baseline chosen from training labels reaches 62.6% holdout accuracy while missing all 64 malignant-labelled examples.
Existing training-only CV and exploratory holdout results; fold SD is not a confidence interval.
All three original saved confusion matrices on the same 171 reused holdout examples.
project.challenge: Accuracy rewards majority guessing on an imbalanced dataset. The useful challenge is to explain which examples were missed and what each denominator means, without turning a reused exploratory holdout into a model-selection claim. The exporter cross-checks independent saved artifacts and carries their hashes into a browser that cannot train, tune or accept patient inputs.
